title: What does the Conductor's icon look like?
lead: Pick the Conductor's mark on the robot icon. I recommend B, a halo of four nodes around its head: it still reads at the smallest size and matches the map, where the orchestrators circle the Conductor. Confidence: medium.
for_you: The helmet keeps showing the model colour; the mark on top shows the role, as the orchestrator's crown does today

for_you.text: An icon swap later is a small change

context: Matt asked for the Conductor (decision 55) to have its own icon. The worker drew three marks on the existing robot (same 48-grid helmets, line weight and glow as robots.js), each shown at 26 px beside today's worker and crowned orchestrator, at 15 px, as a map station plain and red with a count, large, and on all four model helmets.

options.name: Baton
options.summary: A raised baton with a lit tip where the orchestrator wears its crown.
cons: A thin line that gets lost at 15 px

options.name: Halo of nodes
options.summary: A ring of four glowing nodes circling the robot's head.
pros: Reads at 15 px; echoes the map's ring of orchestrators

options.name: Stage arc
options.summary: An arc of three nodes over the robot, standing on a rostrum line.
cons: Busiest of the three at small sizes

recommendation: B stays legible at the smallest size and ties the icon to the map's picture of the Conductor at the centre of its orchestrators.
change_mind: If the halo reads as decoration rather than a role, take A.

images.caption: A: baton, at every size and on every model helmet
B: halo of nodes, at every size and on every model helmet
